label: Bible Study
prompt: I am _____ with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
verse: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
note: Paul's most personal summary of the gospel — 'who loved me' is singular on purpose.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good _____; it is I; be not afraid.
verse: But straightway Jesus spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
note: Spoken across the waves to terrified disciples at night — moments before Peter steps out of the boat.

label: Sunday School
prompt: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup _____ over.
verse: Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies: thou anointest my head with oil; my cup runneth over.
note: Psalm 23's banquet scene: a table set in front of the enemies, and a cup that runneth over.

label: Deep Water
prompt: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore _____ life, that both thou and thy seed may live:
verse: I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:
note: Moses' closing appeal on the plains of Moab: two roads, heaven and earth as witnesses, and a strong hint which to take.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall _____ unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
verse: Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh.
note: To 'cleave' is to stick fast — the Bible's first wedding sermon, later quoted by both Jesus and Paul.
